title: The 4I - E formula for solution architects
oneliner: Investigate, Innovate, Initiate, Implement - minus Ego - equals success as an architect.
says: His formula: investigate the customer's problems, pain points, and modernization journey; innovate with ideas using technologies like IoT, AI, and mobile; initiate the next step, conversation, and action item so deals and projects keep moving; implement the solution cleanly for the customer. Then subtract ego when working with peers and customers.
explained: The four I's map the full arc of an architect's engagement. Investigate comes first because architects who pitch before they understand get politely ignored. Innovate is not about novelty for its own sake - it is bringing the customer options they did not know existed. Initiate is the least technical and most decisive: projects die in the gaps between meetings, and the architect who always sends the follow-up, books the next session, and names the next action is the one whose designs actually get built.

Subtracting ego is the multiplier. Architecture work is persuasion across teams you do not control. The moment the job becomes proving you are the smartest person in the room, people stop bringing you their real constraints - and a design made without the real constraints is fiction.
takeaway: Skills get the design right; initiation gets it built; dropped ego keeps people honest with you. All five parts are required.
